title: Comprehensive curation changes selected lesions but not 3/22 recovery
claim: An explicit all-size plausible-candidate inventory goal was followed for an uncertain benign-favored finding, but the fresh Astra-medium run still localized 3/22 GT instances: it gained follow-up GT14 and lost GT13, explicitly rejected as vascular. Two unmatched low-probability candidates were added. Links remained 1/7 and exact events fell from 2/15 to 1/15 because the newly recovered GT14 event was unresolved. No <=1 mL reference instance was recovered; frozen scientific scores replay exactly.
limitations: New goal, exhaustive-review wording, all-size inclusion and structured uncertainty are bundled.
One new run per condition; stochastic variation and prompt intervention cannot be separated.
GT covers expert-deemed malignant lesions, whereas the new output deliberately includes indeterminate candidates.
Reference agreement is not clinical adjudication; GT used unavailable individual clinical reports.
Candidate probabilities are subjective; the >=0.5 subset assesses reference agreement, not clinical calibration.
A permitted unresolved event is contract-valid but does not match a definite GT event. Exact event agreement does not evaluate the clinical appropriateness of abstention.
Generated or requested planes do not prove attention or adequate target conspicuity; all-size instructions do not guarantee exhaustive search.
Original frozen tasks, scores, masks and references are unchanged. No second curation trial or localized follow-up was launched.
